lines.say: Who lived here three thousand years ago? Five stones answer.
Stone one. Twelve oh eight BCE. An Egyptian pharaoh carves his victories.
Among the names: Israel. Its oldest known mention outside the Bible.
lines.screen: Oldest mention of *Israel* outside the Bible

lines.say: Stone two. Ninth century BCE, at Tel Dan. It names the House of David.
Stone three. Around seven hundred BCE, a tunnel under Jerusalem. The workers sign it in Hebrew.
Stone four is silver. Around six hundred BCE: two tiny scrolls with the priestly blessing.
The oldest Bible text ever found.
Stone five is a coin. One thirty two CE. It reads: for the freedom of Jerusalem.
Other peoples lived here too, and their stones are here as well.
But five stones, across thirteen centuries, keep writing one name.
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
So, who lived here? Ask the stones.

caption_en:
The fifth one fits in your pocket. 🪨

Who lived here 3,000 years ago? Five stones answer.
1️⃣ Merneptah Stele, about 1208 BCE: an Egyptian pharaoh lists his victories. Among the names: Israel. Its oldest known mention outside the Bible. (Egyptian Museum, Cairo)
2️⃣ Tel Dan Stele, 9th century BCE: "the House of David". (Israel Museum)
3️⃣ Siloam inscription, about 700 BCE: workers sign a water tunnel under Jerusalem, in Hebrew. (Istanbul Archaeology Museums)
4️⃣ Ketef Hinnom scrolls, about 600 BCE: two tiny silver scrolls with the priestly blessing, the oldest Bible text ever found. (Israel Museum)
5️⃣ Bar Kokhba revolt coin, 132 to 135 CE: "for the freedom of Jerusalem".

Other peoples lived here too, and their stones are here as well. But five stones, across about 1,340 years, keep writing one name.

Which one surprised you?
caption_he:
מי חי כאן לפני 3,000 שנה? חמש אבנים עונות.
1️⃣ מצבת מרנפתח, בערך 1208 לפנה״ס: פרעה מונה את ניצחונותיו. בין השמות: ישראל. האזכור הקדום ביותר הידוע של ישראל מחוץ לתנ״ך.
2️⃣ כתובת תל דן, המאה ה 9 לפנה״ס: ״בית דוד״.
3️⃣ כתובת השילוח, בערך 700 לפנה״ס: הפועלים חותמים על נקבה מתחת לירושלים, בעברית.
4️⃣ מגילות כתף הינום, בערך 600 לפנה״ס: שתי מגילות כסף זעירות עם ברכת כהנים, טקסט התנ״ך הקדום ביותר שנמצא.
5️⃣ מטבע מרד בר כוכבא, 132 עד 135 לספירה: ״לחרות ירושלים״.
גם עמים אחרים חיו כאן, והאבנים שלהם כאן גם כן. אבל חמש אבנים, לאורך כ 1,340 שנה, כותבות שם אחד.
